title: Agent termination requires a supermajority, a quorum, a minimum voting period and advance public notice
content:
A.1.14.5.1 routes termination through special voting requirements in the Root Edit Primitive, listing four: "a minimum voting period, a minimum quorum, a supermajority approval threshold, and advance notice of the Agent's proposed termination and the subsequent Agent vote issued in the Sky Forum by the Operational Facilitator."

Each targets a distinct failure. A supermajority prevents a bare majority from dissolving an entity others depend on. A quorum blocks a low-turnout capture. A minimum period stops a snap vote executed before opposition can organize. And advance notice — issued by the Facilitator, not the proposer — ensures the announcement reaches the Forum even if the initiators would prefer a quiet vote.

Termination deserves the highest bar because it is the one governance action with no remedy. Every other decision can be revisited by a later vote; dissolution destroys the body that would revisit it, and A.1.14.5.3 confirms the finality by sending undistributable residual assets to Sky Core.

The notice requirement also serves parties who cannot vote at all. Users, counterparties and — under A.1.14.5.2.1 — Prime Agents relying on a terminating Executor need warning long before the wind-down begins, and none of them hold Agent tokens. Making notice a voting *requirement* rather than a courtesy is how the Atlas gives non-voting stakeholders a place in a shareholder decision.
description: Self-dissolution is deliberately harder than ordinary governance; the Operational Facilitator must announce the proposed termination and the vote on the Sky Forum beforehand.
